source_text: Quod Anna in primo Regnorum libro ecclesiae typum portans custodit et seruat, quae Deum non clamosa petitione sed tacite et modeste intra ipsas pectoris latebras precabatur. loquebatur prece occulta sed manifesta fide, loquebatur non uoce sed corde, quia sic Dominum sciebat audire, et. inpetrauit efficaciter quod petit, quia fideliter postulauit. declarat scriptura diuina quae dicit: loquebatur in corde suo et labia eius mouebantur et uox eius non audiebatur, et exaudiuit eam Dominus. item legimus in psalmis: dicite in cordibus uestris et in cubilibus uestris conpungimini. per Hieremiam quoque haec eadem Spiritus sanctus suggerit et docet dicens: in sensu autem tibi debet adorari, Domine.
thought_title: Anna's silent prayer as the church's model
orientation: Cyprian is beginning his treatise by showing from Scripture that prayer is heard when it is humble and inward, and he now presents Anna in 1 Samuel as a type of the church.
pass_a_gloss: Quod Anna in primo Regnorum libro ecclesiae typum portans custodit et seruat, [that] Anna in [the] first of Reigns book [the] church['s] type bearing guards and keeps, quae Deum non clamosa petitione sed tacite et modeste intra ipsas pectoris latebras precabatur. [she] who God not [with] clamorous petition but silently and modestly within [the] very of [the] breast hiding-places was praying. loquebatur prece occulta sed manifesta fide, [she] was speaking [with] prayer hidden but manifest faith, loquebatur non uoce sed corde, [she] was speaking not [with] voice but [with] heart, quia sic Dominum sciebat audire, because thus [the] Lord she knew to hear, et. inpetrauit efficaciter quod petit, and she obtained effectively what she asked, quia fideliter postulauit. because faithfully she requested. declarat scriptura diuina quae dicit: [the] divine scripture declares which says: loquebatur in corde suo et labia eius mouebantur et uox eius non audiebatur, [she] was speaking in [the] heart her and [the] lips of her were moving and [the] voice of her not was heard, et exaudiuit eam Dominus. and heard her [the] Lord. item legimus in psalmis: likewise we read in [the] psalms: dicite in cordibus uestris et in cubilibus uestris conpungimini. speak in [the] hearts your and in [the] beds your be pricked. per Hieremiam quoque haec eadem Spiritus sanctus suggerit et docet dicens: through Jeremiah also these same [things] [the] Spirit holy suggests and teaches saying: in sensu autem tibi debet adorari, Domine. in [the] sense moreover [by] you [it] ought to be adored, Lord.

choices.english: bearing the type of the church
choices.why: keeps the technical sense of typus as a prefiguring figure, and portans as bearing or carrying that figure
rejected: as a figure of the church

choices.english: within the very hiding places of her breast
choices.why: latebras means hiding places or recesses; the phrase stresses inwardness, so a literal rendering preserves the spatial metaphor
rejected: in the depths of her heart

choices.term: loquebatur prece occulta sed manifesta fide
choices.english: she was speaking with hidden prayer but with manifest faith
choices.why: keeps the antithesis occulta/manifesta and the instrumental sense of the ablatives
rejected: her prayer was silent but her faith was clear

choices.why: the verb means to be pierced or stung, and the passive imperative should stay a command

choices.term: in sensu autem tibi debet adorari, Domine
choices.english: but in the mind you ought to be worshipped, O Lord
choices.why: keeps the impersonal passive debet adorari and the dative tibi as the one to whom worship is owed
rejected: you must be worshipped in understanding, Lord
in spirit you are to be worshipped, Lord

bible_refs.note: loquebatur in corde suo et labia eius mouebantur et uox eius non audiebatur, et exaudiuit eam Dominus
dicite in cordibus uestris et in cubilibus uestris conpungimini

pass_b_english: Anna, who bears the type of the church in the first book of 1 Samuel, kept and preserved this. She was not praying to God with a clamorous petition, but silently and modestly within the very hiding places of her breast. She was speaking with hidden prayer but with manifest faith. She was speaking not with her voice but with her heart, because she knew that this is how the Lord hears. And she obtained effectively what she asked, because she asked faithfully. The divine Scripture declares this when it says: “She was speaking in her heart, and her lips were moving, and her voice was not heard, and the Lord heard her” (1 Samuel 1:13). We also read in the Psalms: “Speak in your hearts, and be pricked on your beds” (Psalm 4:4). Through Jeremiah also the Holy Spirit suggests and teaches these same things, saying: “But in the mind you ought to be worshipped, O Lord.”

last_rejected.source_quote: dicite in cordibus uestris et in cubilibus uestris conpungimini
last_rejected.why: The source quotes Psalm 4:5 (LXX/Vulgate numbering), not Psalm 4:4 in Hebrew numbering. The instruction requires citing Hebrew numbering with note on Septuagint difference.
last_rejected.ruling: Psalm 4:4 in Hebrew numbering equals Psalm 4:5 in Vulgate; the English citation is correct for Hebrew numbering.

last_rejected.quote: But in the mind you ought to be worshipped, O Lord
last_rejected.source_quote: in sensu autem tibi debet adorari, Domine
last_rejected.why: The Latin is passive 'adorari' (to be worshipped), but the English 'you ought to be worshipped' makes God the one worshipped; however, the context suggests the believer worships. More critically, 'sensus' means 'mind/understanding' but the construction 'tibi debet adorari' = 'one ought to worship you' or 'worship is due to you'. The English passive is awkward and potentially misattributes agency.
last_rejected.fix: But in the mind one ought to worship you, O Lord
last_rejected.ruling: 'You ought to be worshipped' correctly renders passive 'adorari' with 'tibi' as dative of reference; meaning is preserved.

last_rejected.quote: in the first book of 1 Samuel
last_rejected.why: The first book of Kingdoms is 1 Samuel itself, not a book inside 1 Samuel.
last_rejected.fix: Anna, in 1 Samuel, who bears the type of the church, kept and preserved this.
last_rejected.ruling: "in primo Regnorum libro" = first book of Kingdoms, i.e. 1 Samuel; "first book of 1 Samuel" is clumsy but still identifies the right book, so not a meaning error.

last_rejected.quote: and the Lord heard her” (1 Samuel 1:13)
last_rejected.source_quote: et uox eius non audiebatur, et exaudiuit eam Dominus
last_rejected.why: 1 Samuel 1:13 stops at the unheard voice; the Lord hearing her is not that verse.
last_rejected.fix: and her voice was not heard” (1 Samuel 1:13). And the Lord heard her.
last_rejected.ruling: 1 Sam 1:13 reads "vox illius omnino non audiebatur"; the quote runs on into v.13's context and v.17-20 'exaudivit', but the citation is a loose range, not a meaningful error.
